t.E955.agn: In its 2026 re-evaluation, EFSA maintained the acceptable daily intake (ADI) at 15 mg/kg body weight and reported that even the highest intake estimate was below this limit. Owing to uncertainty about whether chlorinated compounds form at high temperatures, such as in home baking and frying, it did not endorse extending its use in bakery products.
t.E955.body: In humans, only about 9–22% of orally ingested sucralose is absorbed; most of the remainder is excreted in the faeces. Absorbed sucralose is excreted mainly in the urine; less than 10% of what is in the urine is a breakdown product conjugated with glucuronic acid.
t.E955.eff.1.t: It is uncertain whether chlorinated compounds form at high temperatures, such as in home baking and frying
t.E955.eval: In its re-evaluation of 16 February 2026, EFSA did not change the ADI (15 mg/kg body weight/day); it reported that even the highest estimated intake was below this value and that there was no safety concern.
t.E955.prod: A sweetener produced chemically by replacing three hydroxyl groups of sugar (sucrose) with chlorine.
t.E955.summary: A calorie-free sweetener derived from sugar, about 600 times sweeter than sugar. Used in diet drinks and sugar-free products.
t.E955.what: A calorie-free intense sweetener made from sugar.
